record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Examples with the Kakeya rotation property
record.original_question: For dimensions d ≥ 3, are there convex bodies S in R^d other than line segments and d-dimensional balls that still have the Kakeya rotation property?

evidence.quote: Question 9.3. Are there convex bodies S in Rd with d ≥ 3 such that S is not a line segment or a d-dimensional ball, and S has the Kakeya rotation property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let d ≥ 2 be an integer. For a convex body S ⊂ ℝ^d (a compact convex set with non-empty interior, or, more generally, including line segments), say that a convex body K ⊂ ℝ^d is S-Kakeya if, for every rotation ρ ∈ SO(d), K contains a translate of ρ(S). Say that S has the Kakeya rotation property if, for every S-Kakeya convex body K ⊂ ℝ^d and every two congruent copies S₁, S₂ of S contained in K, there exists a continuous family (S_t)_{t ∈ [0,1]} of congruent copies of S, all contained in K, with S_0 = S₁ and S_1 = S₂.

It is known that, in every dimension d ≥ 2, line segments have the Kakeya rotation property, and that d-dimensional Euclidean balls trivially have this property.

Question: For some dimension d ≥ 3, does there exist a convex body S ⊂ ℝ^d, other than a line segment or a d-dimensional ball, that has the Kakeya rotation property?
artifact.status_search_result: The Kakeya rotation property was investigated by Janzer (2022, published in Discrete & Computational Geometry, 2024), who established positive results for line segments in all dimensions and negative results for general convex bodies in dimensions ≥ 4 and stronger negative results in dimension 3. The question of whether any other convex bodies (besides line segments and balls) possess the Kakeya rotation property in d ≥ 3 appears to remain open; no source found resolving it.

status_evidence.title: Rotation inside convex Kakeya sets
status_evidence.snippet: Author shows positive results for line segments in all dimensions, negative answer in d≥4 for general S, and negative for stronger continuous-selection question in d=3.
status_evidence.claim: Known partial results about the Kakeya rotation property; question of further examples not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Rotation Inside Convex Kakeya Sets - DCG
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of Janzer's results on rotation inside convex Kakeya sets.
status_evidence.claim: Current state of the art on this property; no example beyond segments and balls established.
